summary: ```markdown # Render Depth Of Field | Clo 2025.0 Features Deep Dive ## Introduction Hey all you Clovers, it's Phoebe, and I'm going to walk you through this new feature we have for depth of field and one of the improvements we've made for our 2025.0 release. So let's jump on in and have some fun while we learn! ## Understanding Depth of Field For anyone who doesn't know how cameras work—myself included—depth of field helps you understand zooming and focusing. In Clo, you have the option to control this feature from your render window. To access your render window, go to the very top toolbar, select "Render," and then choose "Render." This window will open along with rendering tools, allowing you to see changes in your object browser and property editor, especially in your property editor as you select different tools for your render. ## Accessing Camera Settings In your render window, under the render toolbars, locate the camera icon. Within your property editor, you'll find several options. There's a section labeled "Physical Camera Render Only." If you check this option, you can start to control various settings in your property editor, including depth of field. ## Why Depth of Field Matters You might be wondering why you should care about this feature. Many users create multiple custom views of the same project. When you create custom views—by right-clicking anywhere in your 3D window that's not an avatar or garment—you can adjust various angles. However, if you zoom in a lot on one custom view and zoom out on another, some objects may appear fuzzy, and others may not be sharp. This inconsistency occurs because depth of field averages the focus over many views. ## Customizing Depth of Field What we've done is enable you to tie depth of field settings to each custom view. If you know enough about cameras and want to edit this, you can do so easily. For instance, I'm currently in my first custom view, and I’ll hit "Interactive" for easier adjustments. With "Physical Camera Render Only" checked and exposure on, I can turn on depth of field. Right now, in this custom view, I have it set to "Depth of Field View." However, if you want to adjust the focus, we have a "Focus by Left Click" option. By checking this option, you can easily click where you want the focus to be. ## Example of Focus Adjustment For example, if I want the focus to be on a character in my scene, I can click on her, and the view will automatically update. If I switch to my next custom view and find it a bit blurry, I can simply left-click again to focus on her and see how it adjusts in real-time. Continuing this process, I can go into each custom view and adjust the focus accordingly. The viewpoint focus updates dynamically as I make these adjustments, allowing for precise control over the depth of field. ## Rendering Your Images When you're satisfied with your adjustments, make sure to go to your image settings. You can decide how you want this rendered out. Once everything looks good, you can render your images and see how the sharpness varies based on your selections. The differences in blur and sharpness will clearly show how depth of field has affected your render. ## Conclusion If you're not familiar with the original way of working with depth of field, rest assured that the previous method will still work perfectly for you. This new feature is designed for those who want more control over their rendering. You no longer need to perform multiple renders for different custom views; now you can set everything up in one go. Thank you so much for watching! If you have any questions, use the comment section down below. Don’t forget to like and subscribe, and check out all our other great Clo videos. I hope you had fun! Keep enjoying your experience in Clo! ```
